name: Diary studies and video missions (dscout)
summary: Join occasional paid research 'missions' where you record short videos and answer questions on your phone; this is not a job.
what_you_do: You apply to missions in the dscout app by answering screener questions. If chosen, you complete mission parts, such as recording videos and answering questions about how you use products or go about daily life, and you're paid after the project closes.
who_it_may_fit: You're comfortable recording short phone videos and want occasional, higher-value research missions.
Missions can pay tens to hundreds of dollars each (third-party reviews say about $20 to $200+)
You do it on your phone, on your own schedule within mission deadlines
dscout says it has scouts in the US, the UK and around the world, and the app is listed in the Canadian App Store
who_it_may_not_fit: You need confirmed Canadian access or regular income, or you don't want to film yourself.
No official dscout page confirmed Canada eligibility in this check
Third-party reviews say mission availability depends on your location and demographics
Payment is PayPal only, about two weeks after the project's final mission closes, and you must claim the payment within 30 days
You record videos about your life and habits

conditions_notes: Missions depend on researcher demand and your demographics and location. No volume data was found.

fees: No dscout fee found; PayPal charges a small fee if you ask for a paper cheque instead.
economics_notes: dscout says pay varies with each project's requirements and time. Third-party reviews give about $25–$150 per mission or $20–$200+ per study, without a stated currency basis for Canada.

name: Paid online research studies (Prolific)
summary: Take part in paid online research studies when you match a study's criteria; this is research participation, not a job.
what_you_do: You fill in a demographic profile, then claim studies (mostly surveys and online experiments) that appear in your dashboard on a first-come, first-served basis. Each study lists its reward and estimated time. Once the researcher approves your submission, the reward goes to your balance, which you cash out to PayPal.
who_it_may_fit: You want occasional, flexible small earnings from your computer and can live with unpredictable study supply.
Researchers must pay at least £6 / $8 per hour and are advised to pay £9 / $12 (Prolific rules)
Prolific charges no cash-out fee, and the minimum cash-out is a low £6/$6
You pick studies whenever you like, with no set hours
Long-established platform with a public participant help centre
who_it_may_not_fit: You need dependable weekly income or don't want identity checks and PayPal-only payouts.
Not a job: studies aren't guaranteed, and 2026 third-party reviews say new sign-ups may be waitlisted
Study supply is the most common complaint: some days nothing matches your profile, and popular studies fill fast
The pay rate uses estimated or median completion time, so your real hourly earnings can be lower

Accounts can be put 'On hold' (for example for VPN or location mismatch, many rejections, multiple accounts, or using AI or automation), and Prolific doesn't give a specific reason. You can appeal through support
Payout is PayPal only (through Hyperwallet), in GBP or USD. PayPal may charge for currency conversion, and your PayPal name must match your Prolific details

conditions_notes: Studies are first-come, first-served and depend on your demographics. 2026 reviews describe days with no eligible studies and frequent 'study full' messages. No official supply statistics were found.

advertised_rate.note: Prolific's researcher rules set a minimum reward rate of £6 / $8 per hour and recommend £9 / $12, based on estimated or median completion time. Third-party 2026 reviews report a wide range of effective rates, from about $8–15/hr down to far lower once unpaid waiting and screening time is counted. Rewards are paid in GBP or USD, not CAD.

fees: Prolific charges no cash-out fee (official); PayPal may charge for currency conversion.
economics_notes: Prolific's researcher rules set a minimum reward rate of £6 / $8 per hour and recommend £9 / $12, based on estimated or median completion time. Third-party 2026 reviews report a wide range of effective rates, from about $8–15/hr down to far lower once unpaid waiting and screening time is counted. Rewards are paid in GBP or USD, not CAD.

name: Paid user research sessions (User Interviews)
summary: Apply to occasional paid product-research sessions (interviews, surveys, tests) run by companies; this is research participation, not a job.
what_you_do: You build a participant profile and answer screener surveys for studies that interest you. If a researcher picks you, you join a session such as a video interview or survey and receive an incentive afterwards.
who_it_may_fit: You don't mind filling in screeners now and then for the chance of a well-paid one-off session.
Canada is a supported participant country for projects that User Interviews runs itself ('Recruit' projects)
A single session can pay well for its length (one third-party review reports about US$45 per study on average)
You can redeem incentives in your local currency
who_it_may_not_fit: You need regular income, or you want cash to PayPal or your bank rather than gift cards.
Very occasional: User Interviews itself estimates 1–2 study invitations every 6 months
Screeners can be long, and you may hear nothing for days or weeks (third-party review)
When User Interviews pays you, it's a Tremendous digital gift card or prepaid Visa, not PayPal, Venmo or a bank transfer
Incentives are shown in USD, and one redeemed in the wrong currency can't be reissued
Payment can take up to 10 business days after the session

conditions_notes: Officially, a participant can expect 1–2 invitations every 6 months, and the first selection can take time.

economics_notes: No official average. A third-party review (The Work at Home Woman) reports about US$45 per completed study in its 2026 data, up from $29 in 2021. Each incentive is set by the researcher and varies with study length and type.

name: Website and app tester (UserTesting contributor)
summary: Get paid small amounts to try websites and apps while speaking your thoughts aloud on a screen recording; occasional paid tests, not a job.
what_you_do: You answer screener questions for tests in your dashboard. If you qualify, you complete tasks on a website or app while recording your screen and voice and saying what you think. Every test in your feed shows its pay before you start.
who_it_may_fit: You're comfortable thinking aloud on a recording and want short, occasional paid tasks.
Canada is one of UserTesting's seven standard contributor countries
Pay for each test is shown up front in your feed
Tests are short: third-party reviews commonly cite about $10 for a roughly 20-minute unmoderated test
The practice test can be done in English or French (or German)
who_it_may_not_fit: You need regular income or don't want to be recorded while you talk.
Not a job: screeners often disqualify you, and tests come and go (third-party reviews)
Signing up includes a practice test that reviews describe as unpaid
Payment is PayPal only, about 14 days after each test
If you submit an incomplete test instead of reporting a problem, the payment is cancelled
You have to talk aloud while your screen is recorded

conditions_notes: There's no official data on test volume. Third-party reviews report high screener disqualification rates.

advertised_rate.note: UserTesting's help centre says pay depends on customer demand, test type and tasks, and is shown for each test. Third-party reviews commonly put a typical unmoderated test at about $10, with longer or live sessions paying more (one site advertises $10–$120). The $10 is a typical figure, not a guaranteed minimum.
